% Converted, ltx-talk. C-ONSLIDE-ARG workaround: use a command that really does
% take an argument. \uncover is the right default when converting Beamer's
% \onslide<n>{...} -- it hides but RESERVES the space, so the layout stays stable
% across overlays; \only<n>{...} omits entirely and reserves nothing.
%
% Page counts should be UNCHANGED by this rewrite, which is a good invariant to
% assert. A bare \onslide<2-> with no group is valid ltx-talk and must be LEFT
% ALONE. The mechanical \onslide<spec>{ -> \uncover<spec>{ swap also breaks if the
% group wraps a whole tabular/align*/cases/matrix rather than a cell's contents,
% which is why convert_deck.py deliberately lints for this rather than rewriting.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard=a-4, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\uncover<2>{Revealed on the second overlay.}

Prose that must stay visible on every overlay, including the first.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
